summary: Banc of California completed a transformational reverse merger with PacWest in Nov 2023, absorbed $1.4B goodwill impairment and $442M securities losses in 2023, and spent 2024 executing a $6.1B balance sheet repositioning that pulled out $2.6B BTFP, $1.4B brokered deposits, and $1.95B Civic loans. The 10-K honestly discloses that the repositioning is mostly behind, capital ratios are healthy (CET1 10.55%), and earnings have normalized ($127M for 2024, ~$54M Q1'25). The honest concern is credit migration: classified loans rose from 0.41% to 2.37% of HFI in two years (and the Q1'25 10-Q, filed six days pre-cutoff, shows further +36% QoQ jump to ~3.2%), while ACL coverage of nonaccruals collapsed from 498% to 142%. Office CRE exposure has been genuinely reduced. Auditor change (KPMG to EY) is post-merger lateral, no disagreement. Insider behavior is benign (2 small sales / 46 grants in 15 months). The bank looks like an honest 'boring middle' name working through a real post-merger credit cycle, not a liar hiding distress.
